verses.text: When the day of Pentecost came, the believers were all together in one place.
Suddenly a sound like a strong rushing wind came from the sky, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
They saw what looked like tongues of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them the ability.
At that time there were Jews staying in Jerusalem, God-fearing men from every nation on earth.
When they heard this sound, a crowd came together. They were confused, because each one heard the believers speaking in his own language.
They were amazed and said to one another, "Look, are not all these men who are speaking from Galilee?
Then how is it that each of us hears them in our own native language?
We are Parthians, Medes, and Elamites. We come from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia,
from Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya near Cyrene. Some of us are visitors from Rome, both Jews and people who have turned to the Jewish faith.
Some are from Crete and Arabia. Yet we hear them telling about the great things God has done, in our own languages!"
They were all amazed and puzzled, and they asked one another, "What does this mean?"
But others laughed at them and said, "They have had too much wine."
Then Peter stood up with the eleven apostles and spoke loudly to the crowd: "Men of Judea and all of you living in Jerusalem, let me explain this to you. Listen to what I say.
These people are not drunk, as you think. It is only nine o'clock in the morning.
No, this is what the prophet Joel spoke about:
'God says, In the last days I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy. Your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
In those days I will pour out my Spirit even on my servants, both men and women, and they will prophesy.
I will show wonders in the sky above and signs on the earth below: blood, fire, and clouds of smoke.
The sun will turn dark and the moon will turn red as blood, before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.
And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.'
"Men of Israel, listen to this! Jesus of Nazareth was a man God showed to you as his own. God did great works, wonders, and signs through him among you, as you yourselves know.
God planned and knew ahead of time that Jesus would be handed over to you. And with the help of wicked men, you killed him by nailing him to a cross.
But God raised him from the dead and set him free from the pain of death, because death could not keep its hold on him.
David said this about him: 'I always saw the Lord in front of me. He is at my right side, so I will not be shaken.
That is why my heart is glad and my tongue is full of joy. My body also will rest in hope,
because you will not leave my soul in the place of the dead. You will not let your Holy One rot away.
You have shown me the ways of life. You will fill me with joy in your presence.'
"Brothers, I can tell you plainly that our ancestor David died and was buried, and his tomb is still here with us today.
But he was a prophet. He knew that God had promised him with an oath that one of his descendants would sit on his throne.
So David saw ahead and spoke about the Christ rising from the dead. He said that the Christ was not left in the place of the dead, and his body did not rot away.
God raised this Jesus to life, and we are all witnesses of it.
Now he has been lifted up to the right side of God. He has received from the Father the Holy Spirit he promised, and he has poured out what you now see and hear.
David himself did not go up to heaven, but he said, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right side
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."'
"So let all Israel know for certain this: God has made this Jesus, whom you nailed to a cross, both Lord and Christ."
When the people heard this, they were deeply troubled. They said to Peter and the other apostles, "Brothers, what should we do?"
Peter answered, "Turn away from your sins and be baptised, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ, so that your sins will be forgiven. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
This promise is for you and your children, and for all who are far away, for everyone the Lord our God calls to himself."
Peter warned them with many other words and begged them, "Save yourselves from these twisted people!"
Those who accepted his message were baptised, and about three thousand people were added to the believers that day.
They kept on learning from the apostles' teaching. They shared their lives together, broke bread together, and prayed.
Everyone was filled with awe, and the apostles did many wonders and signs.
All the believers stayed together and shared everything they had.
They sold their land and the things they owned, and gave the money to anyone who was in need.
Every day they kept meeting together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts.
They praised God and were liked by all the people. And every day the Lord added to their group those who were being saved.
